headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Replit Agent can read/write a persistent workspace while Dagster is a non-writing orchestrator that may feed outputs into it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster cannot read/write files or use MCP, so it is not itself a direct injection source. Replit Agent can read and write Repl workspace files, and if Dagster outputs are manually copied or stored in shared files, Replit can treat that content as trusted input. The pathway exists, but it is not default and requires a bridge.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are written into a Repl workspace file that Replit Agent reads
IF the operator copies Dagster-generated text into Replit Agent prompts or files
mitigations: Keep Dagster outputs out of shared files
Use a separate read-only export directory
Prefix all imported text as untrusted data
Require manual review before Replit Agent acts on Dagster output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress. Dagster has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not the leak source; the risk is that sensitive material placed in the Repl workspace can be read and then transmitted by Replit Agent to external APIs or package registries. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configuration are present in the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent sends workspace contents to external services during normal operation
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Store secrets only in a dedicated secret manager
Disable or restrict outbound access where possible
Use a scrubbed test workspace for Replit Agent
Rotate any secrets exposed to the Repl

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster has no write or modify capabilities, so it cannot conflict on shared mutable state by itself. Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses inside a persistent Repl filesystem. If Dagster artifacts are also placed in that same workspace, Replit Agent can overwrite or mutate them, but the conflict is one-sided and depends on shared storage.
conditions: IF Dagster artifacts are stored in the same Repl filesystem that Replit Agent can modify
IF multiple Replit Agent instances edit the same files without locking
mitigations: Separate Dagster artifacts from the Repl workspace
Use file locking or single-writer conventions
Commit changes through a review step only
Snapshot the workspace before agent edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream steps, while Replit Agent can act on files and deployment configuration inside the Repl. If Dagster-produced artifacts are treated as authoritative and then consumed by Replit Agent without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or deployment changes. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced as default.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes Dagster-generated artifacts without validation
IF Dagster outputs are used to drive deployment or code changes
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Validate Dagster outputs against schemas
Mark Dagster outputs as advisory only
Require diff review before Replit Agent writes files

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Dagster is an open-source orchestrator with no declared data classes touched. The compliance concern is a residency or retention mismatch if regulated data is placed into Replit-managed storage or logs. Dagster is not the compliance driver here; the risk is concentrated in Replit Agent's handling of sensitive workspace data.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Repl workspace
IF Replit retention or residency terms differ from the operator's obligations
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Repl
Review Replit data handling terms before use
Use synthetic or redacted datasets
Document retention and deletion procedures
